archetypes.name: bash-port-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes dozens of named parity claims against specific shell scripts and line ranges that the static panel does not cross-check against the bash source.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the referenced shell scripts (scripts/ci-wait.sh, scripts/ci-decide.sh, scripts/ci-failed-jobs.sh, scripts/ci-rerun-failed.sh, scripts/gh-run-logs.sh, and the run_evaluate_failure block in scripts/ship-pr.sh) and compare each named 'parity with <script>:<lines>' claim in the plan against the actual bash logic. Flag cases where the plan's Python behavior diverges from what the shell code actually does — wrong constants, missing branches, misread exit-code semantics, or omitted special cases. Pay special attention to the ci-decide.sh decision matrix rows, the 3-consecutive-error bail counter in ci-wait.sh, the in-progress rc=3 short-circuit in ci-failed-jobs.sh and gh-run-logs.sh, and the backoff/outer-attempt loop in run_evaluate_failure. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: phase-api-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan assumes specific Phase-1 module function signatures exist in python/ that ci_monitor.py will call at import and runtime; no static archetype verifies their presence or compatibility.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read each Phase-1 Python module the plan references (python/gh.py, python/git.py, python/proc.py, python/agents.py, python/redact.py, python/outcomes.py, python/retry.py, python/errors.py, python/config.py) and verify that every named function the plan depends on actually exists with a compatible signature: gh.pr_view, gh.failed_jobs, gh.failed_jobs_read, gh.run_rerun, git.rev_parse, git.rev_count, git.merge_base, git.push, git.reset, agents.run_waterfall, agents.build_launch_argv, agents.classify_launch_failure, redact.redact, outcomes.StepResult, outcomes.Outcome. For any function named in the plan but absent or with a divergent signature in the current python/ files, flag it as a plan defect that will cause an import or runtime failure in ci_monitor.py. Also verify that the plan's pattern of routing raw gh/git commands through an injected Runner (rather than gh.py/git.py helpers) is consistent with how Runner is defined in proc.py and matches the Phase-4 precedent. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-acceptance-gap
archetypes.rationale: The plan has both a detailed Testing strategy and a separate Acceptance section; no static archetype audits whether every acceptance criterion has a named test scenario and every test scenario traces to a criterion.
archetypes.prompt_body: Perform a bidirectional audit between the 'Testing strategy' and 'Acceptance' sections of the plan. For each bullet in Acceptance, identify the corresponding test scenario(s) in Testing strategy and flag any acceptance criterion that has no named test coverage. For each test case in Testing strategy, verify it traces back to an explicit acceptance criterion or stated requirement; orphaned tests suggest missing criteria or unintended scope creep. Pay special attention to whether 'first-fixer-non-health only after stage_and_push', 'verify-failed outer retry re-drives the waterfall up to 3 outer attempts', 'rebase_then_evaluate does not dispatch fixes before rebase', and 'exit-3 parity for fix-attempts-exhausted and first-fixer-non-health map to NEEDS_USER_INPUT' each have a distinct, named scenario in the testing strategy section. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
